title: Finite etale schemes have effective fppf descent
statement: Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $\{T_i\to T\}_{i\in I}$ be an fppf covering [def-pc-fppf-site], with all schemes and indexing sets in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Write $\mathsf{FEt}(U)$ for the category of finite etale $U$-schemes and all $U$-morphisms [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-etale-morphism]. A descent datum consists of $X_i\in\mathsf{FEt}(T_i)$ and isomorphisms $\phi_{ij}:X_i\times_TT_j\xrightarrow{\sim}T_i\times_TX_j$ over $T_i\times_TT_j$ satisfying $\phi_{ik}=\phi_{jk}\circ\phi_{ij}$ after pullback to triple overlaps [def-pc-fibre-product, def-trf-scheme-cover-descent-datum]. Its morphisms are families of $T_i$-morphisms commuting with the overlap isomorphisms. Pullback is an equivalence from $\mathsf{FEt}(T)$ to this category of descent data. In particular every such datum is induced by a finite etale $T$-scheme $X$, with compatible isomorphisms $X\times_TT_i\simeq X_i$, and every compatible family of morphisms between two pulled-back objects descends to a unique $T$-morphism. No quasi-compactness or noetherian hypothesis on $T$, and no nonemptiness or constant-rank hypothesis on the $X_i$, is imposed.

proof.text: For a finite etale $T$-scheme $X$, each $X\times_TT_i\to T_i$ is finite etale by [def-weil-pbc-finite-etale-category]. Identify both iterated pullbacks on an overlap with $X\times_T(T_i\times_TT_j)$ using [def-pc-fibre-product]. Their comparison defines the canonical overlap isomorphism. On triple overlaps both composites retain the same $X$ coordinate and ordered base coordinates, so are equal by the uniqueness in the fibre-product universal property. The same uniqueness shows that base change of any $T$-morphism commutes with the comparisons and preserves identities and composition. Thus pullback defines the stated functor.

source.place: Tag 0BLZ (examples-stacks.tex, lemma-finite-etale-stack); pullback comparisons in Tag 023V (definition-descent-datum)

proof.text: The covering is fpqc by [lem-trf-fppf-covering-is-fpqc]. For two finite etale $T$-schemes $X,Y$ and compatible maps $b_i:X\times_TT_i\to Y\times_TT_i$, compose $b_i$ with projection to $Y$. By the stated compatibility these maps agree on $(X\times_TT_i)\times_X(X\times_TT_j)\simeq X\times_TT_i\times_TT_j$; this identification uses [def-pc-fibre-product]. The family $X\times_TT_i\to X$ is fpqc by [lem-galois-fpqc-covering-base-change]. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent], with target scheme $Y$, gives a unique map $b:X\to Y$. Its composite to $T$ equals the structure map of $X$: the two agree after this covering, so uniqueness in the same descent lemma, now with target $T$, makes them equal. The pullback of $b$ to $T_i$ equals $b_i$ because their projections to both $Y$ and $T_i$ agree. This proves full faithfulness for all morphisms, without an invertibility condition.

Now fix a datum $(X_i,\phi_{ij})$. Apply [lem-trf-fppf-family-coproduct-descent-encoding] to form $A=\coprod_iT_i$, $Z=\coprod_iX_i$, and its singleton datum $D$ over $A/T$. That statement supplies both the fpqc covering $A\to T$ and the equivalence of effectivity with the original family datum. The map $Z\to A$ is affine: each $X_i\to T_i$ is affine by [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]; choose affine open covers of the $T_i$. Their images form an affine open cover of $A$ by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family], and their inverse images in $Z$ are the corresponding affine opens of $X_i$. Thus [pqf-lem-affine-local-target] applies. This uses no finiteness of $I$ and makes no assertion that $A\to T$ is quasi-compact.

Apply [lem-galois-fpqc-affine-descent-effective] to the singleton fpqc covering $A\to T$ and the affine $Z\to A$ with datum $D$. Its conclusion gives a scheme $X\to T$ and an isomorphism $X\times_TA\simeq Z$ respecting the canonical datum. The last assertion of [lem-trf-fppf-family-coproduct-descent-encoding] restricts this to isomorphisms $X\times_TT_i\simeq X_i$ respecting every $\phi_{ij}$. Thus the given family datum is effective as a scheme datum.

The original family is fpqc by [lem-trf-fppf-covering-is-fpqc]. Under the isomorphisms just obtained, every base change $X\times_TT_i\to T_i$ is finite and etale. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-descend-finite] to $X\to T$ and this family to deduce finiteness; apply [lem-galois-fpqc-descend-etale] to the same morphism and family to deduce etaleness. Hence $X$ lies in $\mathsf{FEt}(T)$ and the functor is essentially surjective.

For completeness, choose a preimage $X_D$ and an isomorphism $a_D:F(X_D)\simeq D$ for each datum $D$ in the fixed universe. Send $u:D\to E$ to the unique map whose image is $a_E^{-1}ua_D$, using full faithfulness from Step 2. Uniqueness proves the identity and composition laws; the $a_D$ are natural by this formula. Full faithfulness also lifts $a_{F(X)}:F(X_{F(X)})\simeq F(X)$ and its inverse, giving a natural isomorphism from this inverse functor composed with $F$ to the identity. This proves equivalence. Empty covers force $T$ empty and give the unique empty scheme; empty $X_i$ and ranks varying on components require no change to Steps 1--5. No quasi-compactness or noetherian condition on $T$ was used.
